name: Feeding America: policy, research and awareness (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: Feeding America's US food policy advocacy, research and awareness.
summary: Feeding America's policy and advocacy, research (Map the Meal Gap) and public awareness programmes ($49 million in the year to June 2025, $45 million a year on average over the five years to then in 2025 prices) campaign with the rest of the anti-hunger coalition to protect and expand federal food programmes. Counted as a past average over those five years, three wins carry lasting federal food money: the 2021 re-evaluation of the Thrifty Food Plan (about $17 billion a year of SNAP benefits), permanent Summer EBT ($2.7 billion a year) and the smaller SNAP cut in the 2025 budget law than the House passed (about $10 billion a year). Valued for the households who get it net of what it costs the taxpayers who fund it, with 5% to 25% of each win caused by the coalition, a quarter of the coalition's resources Feeding America's, and its next dollar at 39% of the average, a dollar does about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000. It is low because the money goes to US households only a few times poorer per person than those who pay, and because the coalition caused only a small share of it. The result is mostly uncertainty (whether the coalition caused any of the money is a judgment spanning ten-fold), and it is discounted for missing data.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

sections.title: Career changes
sections.explainer: People the charity moves into high-impact jobs: per career changed, the pay they give up for the years they stay, valued at the new employer's live result per dollar, times the share of changes the charity caused (docs/normalization.md 2.8). The mirror of staff pay below market.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Value of the career changes (units of value)
Thrifty Food Plan: share of the rise that wouldn't have come at all, or not for years, without the anti-hunger coalition
rows.explainer: The research on whether advocacy changes policy: Baumgartner, Berry, Hojnacki, Kimball and Leech (2009, Lobbying and Policy Change, 98 random US federal issues) find about 60% of campaigns change nothing, the status quo usually wins and resources explain under 5% of who wins; organised constituent contact moves a legislator's support by about 12 points (Bergan and Cole 2015). The re-evaluation was ordered by the 2018 farm bill, which the coalition pressed for, and carried out by USDA under an administration that wanted it; the coalition's research and comments shaped its size. 0.12, range 0.03 to 0.3, below the Habitat advocacy build's 0.15 for local housing money, since the decision was the administration's.

rows.label: Summer EBT: share that wouldn't have come at all, or not for years, without the anti-hunger coalition
rows.explainer: The research on whether advocacy changes policy: Baumgartner, Berry, Hojnacki, Kimball and Leech (2009, Lobbying and Policy Change, 98 random US federal issues) find about 60% of campaigns change nothing, the status quo usually wins and resources explain under 5% of who wins; organised constituent contact moves a legislator's support by about 12 points (Bergan and Cole 2015). Summer EBT was the coalition's own campaign for a decade (demonstrations from 2011, pandemic EBT, then a permanent programme in the December 2022 appropriations law); without it the programme would at best have come years later. 0.25, range 0.05 to 0.5, above the Habitat build's 0.15 as a campaign the coalition led.

rows.label: 2025 budget law: share of the cut left out that the coalition caused
rows.explainer: The research on whether advocacy changes policy: Baumgartner, Berry, Hojnacki, Kimball and Leech (2009, Lobbying and Policy Change, 98 random US federal issues) find about 60% of campaigns change nothing, the status quo usually wins and resources explain under 5% of who wins; organised constituent contact moves a legislator's support by about 12 points (Bergan and Cole 2015). The Senate's smaller cut followed the parliamentarian's rulings, budget targets and senators' own states (Alaska's carve-out) as much as advocacy; the coalition's calls (Feeding America counts a million advocacy actions) may have moved a few senators. 0.05, range 0.01 to 0.2.

rows.label: How much of the money and its reach is real and specific to these wins
rows.explainer: The money figures are official (GAO, CRS) except the 2025 difference, which is Feeding America's reading of two bills; Summer EBT's spending grows as states join, the re-evaluation could be partly reversed by a later law (persistence is in $win_years_counted, not here). 0.85, range 0.6 to 1.

rows.label: Feeding America's share of the resources of the coalition behind the wins
rows.explainer: The anti-hunger coalition: Feeding America ($45 million a year on these three lines on average), the member food banks' own advocacy and Feeding America Action, the Food Research and Action Center and Share Our Strength (each smaller on federal policy than Feeding America), the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities (a large think tank of which SNAP is one subject), faith groups, unions, and states' agencies. Feeding America is the largest single funder of this work and the food banks' voice, but a minority of the whole: 0.25, range 0.1 to 0.5.

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of the households' gross value
rows.explainer: (+) children's long-run gains from food benefits in childhood, beyond the year's consumption: adult health and economic self-sufficiency (Hoynes, Schanzenbach and Almond 2016, American Economic Review; Bailey et al. 2024), +5%; (+) Map the Meal Gap and the network's data help food banks put food where need is greatest, +2%; (+) wins that carry no money (school meal rules, SNAP access for students), +1%; (-) benefits that reduce work a little, about 0. 8%, range -5% to +25%.

rows.label: Total units of value
rows.formula: tfp_value * tfp_total_adj + sebt_value * sebt_total_adj + obbba_value * obbba_total_adj + unmodelled_benefits_adj * (tfp_gross_value * tfp_total_adj + sebt_gross_value * sebt_total_adj + obbba_gross_value * obbba_total_adj) + moved_value + careers_value
rows.explainer: Each win's net value after its own adjustments, plus the unmodelled share of the households' gross value.
